Title: Batangas Barako (Liberica)
Body (HTML):
Grown in the volcanic soil around Mt. Batulao, barako is the coffee your lola brewed before "specialty coffee" was a phrase anyone used. Liberica beans give it a bold, almost meaty aroma and a flavor that leans dark chocolate and tobacco, with a low acidity that lets the body carry the cup.

This is the taste Batangueños have been proud of for generations, thick, dark, and unapologetically strong. Best brewed the old way: french press or moka pot, no sugar required.

Title: Benguet Arabica
Body (HTML):
High in the Cordillera mountains, Benguet's cool climate and mineral-rich soil produce arabica beans with a bright, floral character rare for Philippine coffee. Notes of black cherry and brown sugar unfold over a clean, tea-like body.

Farmed on small terraced plots alongside Benguet's famous vegetable gardens, this lot is washed and sun-dried to bring out its natural sweetness. A cup that rewards a slow pour-over morning.

Title: Sagada Arabica
Body (HTML):
Sagada's fog-covered slopes and steep elevation give this arabica a lively citrus snap, think green apple and honey over a delicate, tea-like body. It's one of the brightest cups we roast.

Grown by smallholder farmers in the Cordillera's pine forests, Sagada beans are prized for their clarity. Try it cold-brewed to let the fruit notes really sing.
Tags: medium-roast, citrusy, honeyed, bright-acidity, sagada, arabica

Title: Mt. Apo Arabica
Body (HTML):
Grown on the slopes of the Philippines' highest peak, Mt. Apo arabica thrives at elevations most Philippine coffee never reaches. The result is a complex, well-balanced cup with ripe berry and cacao nib notes and a natural cane-sugar sweetness.

Harvested by farming communities around Mt. Apo, this lot is roasted lightly to preserve its fruit-forward character. A coffee for slowing down with.
Tags: light-roast, berry-notes, cacao, balanced, mt-apo, arabica, davao

Title: Kalinga Robusta
Body (HTML):
Kalinga robusta is grown in the rugged highlands of the Cordillera, where the beans develop a bold, nutty intensity that stands up to milk, sugar, or a double shot of espresso. Expect dark chocolate and roasted nut flavors with an earthy backbone.

This is a working coffee, the kind farmers and market vendors have relied on for its punch and affordability. Dark roasted for maximum body and crema.
Tags: dark-roast, nutty, earthy, bold, robusta, kalinga

Title: Kapihan House Blend
Body (HTML):
Our house blend brings together Batangas barako and Benguet arabica for a cup that's familiar and balanced, the kind you'd be served at any kapihan along the highway. Toasted almond and caramel sweetness sit over a smooth, medium body.

Consistent, versatile, and built for everyday brewing, whether that's a drip pot at sunrise or a moka pot after merienda.

Title: Ceramic Pour-Over Dripper
Body (HTML):
A simple, one-piece ceramic dripper designed for slow, even extraction. The spiral ridges and single large hole give you full control over your pour-over brew time, so you can pull out every note in a light-roast single origin.

Glazed in a warm terracotta finish that echoes our own brand colors, it's built to last through years of unhurried mornings.

Title: Filipino Cloth Coffee Sock Filter
Body (HTML):
Long before pour-over cones, Filipino households brewed coffee through a cloth "sock" strainer, and the method still makes some of the smoothest, sediment-free coffee around. Ours is sewn from tightly woven cotton flannel with a sturdy wire rim.

Reusable, easy to rinse, and gentle on any grind, it's a low-tech tool that's stood the test of generations of kapihan mornings.
